LESSON: VEGETATION IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Vegetation in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Vegetation in Eastern Africa, part of Strand 1 in Grade 6 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we conserve vegetation in our environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm, in pairs, the main types of vegetation in Eastern Africa, and share in class,

2. draw a map of Eastern Africa indicating the main types of vegetation and display the map class,

3. discuss the characteristics of the main types of vegetation in Eastern Africa,

4. plan and carry out activities on conservation of vegetation in the locality.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm, in pairs, the main types of vegetation in Eastern Africa, and share in class,
2. draw a map of Eastern Africa indicating the main types of vegetation and display the map class,
3. discuss the characteristics of the main types of vegetation in Eastern Africa,
4. plan and carry out activities on conservation of vegetation in the locality.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Vegetation in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: Learners follow instructions to locate the main vegetation types in Eastern Africa

using digital devices.

● Self-Efficacy: Learners identify general features in their locality as they plan and carry out activities on conservation of

vegetation,

Link to

Values:
● Responsibility: Learners show determination as they plant and care for vegetation at school.

● Peace: Learners respect self and others as they discuss, in groups, the characteristics of the main types of vegetation in

Eastern Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PICs):

● Environmental education: Learners practise environmental awareness as they plan and write down, in groups, how

they will conserve vegetation within the school compound.

● Patriotism: Learners demonstrate patriotism as they plan and carry out activities on conservation of vegetation in

their locality.

Links to other Learning Areas:
● Learners apply Integrated Science knowledge and skills to plant and care for vegetation at school.

● Learners use Creative Arts skills to draw and display in class a map showing the main types of vegetation in Eastern

Africa.
